extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office examiners; patent applicants and practitioner counsel interacting with appeals and judicial review
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and examiner guidance governing dismissal of appeals, handling of claims when appeals are dismissed or decisions are returned from courts/boards, and requirements for seeking judicial review (appeals/civil actions) of PTAB decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because no brief was filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal stands dismissed by operation of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss until any available extension to file the brief has expired (e.g., up to 5 months of extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a)), unless appellant specifically withdraws the appeal as to rejected claims. Applications with no allowed claims will be abandoned. Claims indicated as allowable except for dependency from rejected claims are to be treated as if they were rejected. If an amendment obviously places the application in condition for allowance (with supervisory concurrence per MPEP § 1002.02(d)), the primary examiner may recommend entry of the amendment. Examiner should follow the provided examples (A–D) about canceling rejected claims and issuing application on allowed claims, or holding the application abandoned where appropriate. If formal matters remain, the examiner may handle them by examiner's amendment (MPEP § 1302.04) or use form paragraph 12.209 to require corrections within a shortened statutory period; prosecution is otherwise closed except as to such formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 12.209 — Appeal Dismissed; allowed claims with formal matters remaining
rubrics_metrics.description: Template/form paragraph to notify applicant that the appeal stands dismissed, that allowed claim(s) will be passed to issue provided certain formal matters are corrected, and to set a shortened statutory period for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when formal matters cannot be handled by examiner's amendment. Insert mailing date and describe formal matters to be corrected in bracket 2. Require corrections within TWO (2) MONTHS to avoid abandonment; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 may be granted but cannot extend reply beyond statutory maximum SIX MONTHS (35 U.S.C. 133). Include Examiner Notes: use only if notice of appeal filed on/after Jan 23, 2012; form-specific bracket instructions; reminder that claims allowable except for dependency are considered rejected (see MPEP § 1215.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because brief was held non-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal will be dismissed if an applicant fails to timely and fully reply to a notice of noncompliance with 37 CFR 41.37(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no allowed claims remain, the application is abandoned as of the date the reply was due. Applicant may petition to revive and to reinstate the appeal (petition must show equivalent evidence to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137). If the appeal is dismissed but allowed claims remain, the application is not abandoned; reinstating claims cancelled by examiner because of dismissal requires a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 and a showing equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137. A proper reply to the notice of noncompliance must be filed before the petition will be considered on its merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal because appeal forwarding fee was not paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal forwarding fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) is not paid within the period set forth in 37 CFR 41.45(a), the appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences mirror failure-to-file-brief: applications with no allowed claims will be abandoned; claims allowable except for dependency treated as if rejected. Examiner may recommend entry of amendment that places application in condition for allowance (subject to supervisory concurrence). Examiner should follow same illustrative examples (A–D) and may handle formal matters by examiner's amendment or form paragraph 12.209; prosecution closed except as to such formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal as to claims subjected to new grounds of rejection in examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.39(a)(2)), appellant must timely respond or the appeal as to those claims may be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must, within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer, either (1) request prosecution be reopened by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111, or (2) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 addressing each new ground of rejection. Failure to do so permits sua sponte dismissal of the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection. Examiner may use form paragraph 12.279.02 to notify appellant that the appeal as to specified claims is dismissed and those claims are canceled; indicate remaining claims and forward application to the Board as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal following remand — substitute examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after remand from the Board, the appellant fails to timely and fully reply to a substitute examiner’s answer (written in response to a remand under 37 CFR 41.50(a)(1)), the appeal may be dismissed as to claims subject to the remanded rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 41.50(a)(1), appellant must within two months from the date of the substitute examiner’s answer either (1) request prosecution be reopened by filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.111, or (2) request that the appeal be maintained by filing a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41. Failure to timely and fully reply permits dismissal as to the claims for which the Board remanded the proceeding and cancellation of those claims. Examiner may use form paragraph 12.286 to inform the appellant of options and to document dismissal of specified claims while leaving other claims alive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims 'allowable except for dependency' (dependent-claim rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims indicated as containing allowable subject matter but objected to as being dependent upon a rejected claim are to be considered as if they were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is reiterated in multiple dismissal/issuance contexts: dependent claims objected as allowable because of dependency are treated as rejected for purposes of abandonment/dismissal and for determining whether any claims remain allowable. Examiners should follow MPEP § 1215.04 when deciding whether to cancel, convert, or hold the application abandoned due to such dependent-claim situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review routes and waiver consequences (35 U.S.C. 141, 145, 306, 318/328, 146)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with a final written decision of the PTAB may seek judicial review either by appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141) or by civil action in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia (35 U.S.C. 145); filing an appeal to the Federal Circuit waives the right to proceed under section 145.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination appeal rights and post-grant/inter partes review appeals are limited to the Federal Circuit (see 35 U.S.C. 306, 318(a), 328(a)). In derivation proceedings a party may appeal to the Federal Circuit under 35 U.S.C. 141 or may file a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 146; an adverse party may elect to have proceedings conducted under section 146, which can affect dismissal of a Federal Circuit appeal if the appellant does not commence a civil action within required times. Parties should be aware of these exclusive routes and the waiver consequences of choosing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements for appeals (37 CFR 90.2 and related rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of appeal required by 35 U.S.C. 142 must be filed with the Director per § 104.2; a copy must also be filed with the Patent Trial and Appeal Board per 37 CFR 41.10(a), 41.10(b), or 42.6(b). The party must comply with Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure and Federal Circuit rules, including serving requisite copies and paying fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: appeals from ex parte reexamination must conform to § 1.550(f); appeals from IPR, PGR, CBM, or derivation proceedings must include sufficient information to allow the Director to determine whether to intervene (35 U.S.C. 143) and must be served per § 42.6(e). For elections under 141(d) and notices of election under 146, file and serve per § 104.2 and § 42.6(b)/(e) as applicable. For filing to be timely in the USPTO, the notice must actually reach the USPTO within time specified in 37 CFR 90.3 or be mailed by Priority Mail Express® per 37 CFR 1.10 (date-accepted treated as filing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director / Office of the Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of papers filed in court proceedings in which the Director is a party must be served on the Office of the Solicitor, not on the Director, Board, or examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service may be effected: (A) by hand between 8:30 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. EST to Office of the Solicitor, 600 Dulany Street, Madison West Building, Room 8C43, Alexandria, VA; or (B) by mail to Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Do not supplement the mail-service address to refer to the Director or USPTO. Any noncourt papers mailed to this mail-service address will be returned to sender; that address is only for court papers. Court-service copies are deemed served when actually received in the Office of the Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing notice of appeal or commencing civil action (37 CFR 90.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines: For appeals under 35 U.S.C. 141 and for commencing civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146, the notice of appeal or civil action must be filed no later than sixty-three (63) days after the date of the final Board decision (subject to rules for specific statutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time computation rules: a timely request for rehearing resets the time for appeal/civil action to no later than 63 days after action on the rehearing request; subsequent rehearing requests normally do not reset the time unless ordered by Board. If the last day falls on a Federal holiday in D.C., time extended per 35 U.S.C. 21(b). Cross-appeal timing is controlled by Federal Rules (e.g., Rule 4(a)(3) FRAP) and Federal Circuit rules. For notices to be timely in the PTO, actual receipt or Priority Mail Express® date-accepted rules apply (see 37 CFR 1.10 and 90.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time to seek judicial review (37 CFR 90.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may extend the time for filing an appeal or commencing civil action upon written request: (A) before expiration for good cause; or (B) after expiration upon a showing of excusable neglect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be filed as provided in § 104.2. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(b), 1.550(c), and fee extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not available to extend the time to seek judicial review once a decision or a decision on rehearing has been entered. To expedite handling, a copy of the extension request may be provided to the Office of the Solicitor (Mail Stop 8). Time periods specified in 37 CFR 90.3 are calendar days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of application and amendments during judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: During judicial review the administrative file will not be opened to the public by the USPTO unless otherwise available; the application or reexamination is not under the jurisdiction of the examiner or the Board unless remanded by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment can be admitted only under the provisions of 37 CFR 1.198. Ex parte reexamination and other special rules (see MPEP § 1214.07 for remand/amendment handling) apply. Parties should be aware that USPTO generally lacks authority to act in ways that would conflict with the court's jurisdiction during judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure following decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (mandate entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Federal Circuit decides an appeal, the court issues a certified copy of its decision (the 'mandate') which is entered in the file; the date the mandate was issued marks the conclusion of the appeal (termination of proceedings per 35 U.S.C. 120).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions depend on whether all claims were rejected, some claims allowed, remand required, or prosecution reopened: - All claims rejected: proceedings considered terminated on mandate issue date; application ordinarily not open to amendment or revival by USPTO (send notice of abandonment unless mandate indicates further action). - Some claims allowed: proceedings terminated only as to claims still rejected; dependent claims previously objected as allowable because of dependency are treated as rejected. Examiner should either (1) convert dependent claims to independent form by examiner's amendment, cancel claims in which rejection was affirmed, and issue application; or (2) set a 2-month time limit for appellant to rewrite dependent claims in independent form (extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) available). If no timely reply, application is abandoned. If formal matters remain, examiner should promptly handle them (examiner's amendment or setting a 2-month shortened statutory period). Examiner should set forth reasons for allowance, referring to and incorporating appellate brief and court decision (see MPEP § 1302.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand handling when court decision raises unconsidered merits issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the court's decision brings up claims or issues not previously considered on the merits (e.g., reversal of rejection for generic claims in nonelected species), the examiner will take the case up for appropriate action on those matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should follow standard procedures for reopening prosecution, remand responses, and any necessary amendments or examiner actions consistent with the court's mandate and applicable USPTO rules (see MPEP § 1216 discussion and MPEP § 1214.07 for handling post-remand amendments).
